subject.title: [Feature]: SSRF 内网访问确认机制

question: Should OpenClaw add a browser private-network SSRF confirmation or allow/block policy, and which core policy shape is approved for browser navigation?
rationale: The request changes a security boundary and public config surface, and current code has no existing confirmation or temporary-grant contract that automation can extend safely without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design a staged core policy
options.body: Approve a narrow first phase such as explicit allow/block policy plus non-overridable metadata blocking before deciding whether interactive confirmation belongs in core.

options.title: Approve interactive confirmation
options.body: Commit to a user-approval UX with timeout, rate-limit, audit, redirect, and WebSocket semantics across browser navigation paths before implementation.

options.title: Keep current strict model
options.body: Decline new core policy surface for now and document that private-network browser access remains either strict deny, hostname exceptions, or explicit broad trusted-environment opt-in.

recommendation.title: Design a staged core policy
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow first phase such as explicit allow/block policy plus non-overridable metadata blocking before deciding whether interactive confirmation belongs in core.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the recent strict browser SSRF behavior that this issue would extend.
